title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

errors: The figure's top label appears to read τ_0τ_1 r = ρ_∞ r, while the text gives τ_0τ_1 r = ρ_∞^{-1} r (and τ_1τ_0 r = ρ_∞ r). This is a minor labeling slip; the text version is the consistent one.

The margin attributes 'changes the vertex of type i, fixes the other two' to σ_i, while the figure and text use τ_i for the same reflections. This is a notational inconsistency with the previous page (σ_i), not a mathematical error.

The phrase 'the orientations ... defined by r and r′ respectively, are opposite' is correct for surface orientations, but sits awkwardly next to 'the induced orientations are the same' on the common side. The two statements refer to different objects (the surface versus the shared side), so there is no contradiction.

ideas.what: Encoding of maps by flags (triangles of the barycentric subdivision) with three involutions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞, where τ_i changes the type-i vertex.
ideas.modern_name: Flag-system / cartographic group description of maps (C_2 = ⟨σ_0,σ_1,σ_2 | σ_i²=(σ_0σ_2)²=1⟩)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978), Malgoire–Voisin (1977), Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); earlier Tutte and others for flags
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §3 on cartographic groups

ideas.what: Rotations ρ_i as products of two reflections, fixing the vertex of type i, with ρ_1² = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Oriented cartographic group C_2^+ ≅ Z * Z/2 (related to PSL_2(Z)); dessins/hypermap monodromy

ideas.what: Convention check: adjacent flags induce the same orientation on their common side but opposite rotation senses around shared vertices; sides oriented (0,1), (1,∞), (∞,0).
ideas.modern_name: Orientation conventions for flags / chamber systems

ideas.what: Counting the 9 flags at distance ≤ 2 from r, with the deficit from 10 explained by the relation (τ_0τ_∞)² = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Ball of radius 2 in the Cayley graph of the cartographic group acting on flags

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine local picture of the cartographic-group/flag formalism for maps. The material is well known: Grothendieck published it in Esquisse d'un programme, and Jones–Singerman and Malgoire–Voisin developed it independently. Nothing on the page goes beyond that.
transcription_corrections: The final parenthesis reads '(il y aurait 10 repères, au lieu de 9 = 1+3+(2+1+2), s'il n'y avait ici la relation τ_0τ_∞ = τ_∞τ_0 i.e. ρ_1 = ρ_1^{-1} i.e. ρ_1² = 1)'. The '9' is written explicitly in the image.

The figure label 'τ_1τ_∞ r = ρ_0^{-1} r' is not legible in the figure. The visible lower-left label reads 'τ_1τ_0 r = ρ_0^{-1} r', apparently a slip for τ_1τ_∞ r = ρ_0^{-1} r as in the text list. The left label reads 'τ_∞τ_1 r = ρ_0 r'.
In the text list, the line containing 'ρ_1 r = τ_∞τ_0 r = ρ_1^{-1} r' should be read as 'τ_0τ_∞ r = ρ_1 r = τ_∞τ_0 r = ρ_1^{-1} r'.
'déduits par 'W' figures' is likely 'déduits par une ou deux fois les opérations τ_i' (the flags are obtained by applying the τ_i once, then composing once more).
